problems.title: Preserve allocation ownership when two allocators share a process
problems.summary: The allocator proxy must distinguish memory owned by oneTBB from allocations made elsewhere in the process. Issue #210 reports a crash in a macOS application using allocation interposition.

commits.title: Check allocator ownership against currently live regions
Index live regions for logarithmic ownership lookups

fix.why_together: The first commit provides the ownership check and interoperability coverage. The second depends on it and replaces the linear scan in the allocation path with a balanced, allocation-free index. Both are required for the tested, scalable repair.

tests: CMake Release targets tbbmalloc and test_malloc_whitebox
validation.detail: 8 cases and 10,349,356 assertions passed. The full oneTBB build, other CTest targets and macOS were outside this run. Tested dogfood commit f1e4e4b1bbef6e3b02e12d8c8022140df6f986f8.

draft.title: Preserve allocation ownership when two allocators share a process
draft.body:
**Summary.** A process can use oneTBB and its original allocator at the same time. Existing upstream report #210 describes a crash with allocator interposition on macOS. Whether that application has the same underlying cause remains unverified.

**Expected behavior.** Memory remains associated with the allocator that owns it, including as allocator regions are added or released.

**Compatibility check.** On the repaired tree, configure a Release build with `TBB_TEST=ON`, build `tbbmalloc` and `test_malloc_whitebox`, and run `ctest -R '^test_malloc_whitebox$'`. The suite checks ordinary mixed allocations, region boundaries and index consistency. All eight cases passed on Ubuntu 26.04.1 x86-64, AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, GCC 15.2.0.

**Fix.** Check ownership against live allocator regions while holding the region lock, then validate the allocator’s back-reference. An allocation-free balanced index keeps that lookup logarithmic as the number of live regions grows.
